scientific_conclusion: QTEMP measures observable decoded-waveform temporal discontinuity patterns; it does not identify packet loss, network failure, buffering, concealment, missing speech, or a physiological cause. Dropout-like events remain ambiguous at natural pause boundaries.
The four preserved outputs reconstruct deterministically from frozen event ledgers and eligible exposure; valid zero, unavailable status, duration burden, and event frequency remain distinct.
The native decoded signal view, channel handling, preprocessing order, parameters, tests, media provenance, and immutable artifact hashes are pinned and verified.
Registered gain, polarity, common-time-shift, native-view, and sample-rate behavior is characterized; unsupported signal-chain equivalence claims are prohibited.

Synthetic and participant-disjoint real-speech injections recover registered dropout-like and near-exact repetition targets, but this validates controlled observables rather than real-world physical causes.

Pause boundaries, stop closures, ordinary silence, periodic speech, and other natural speech structure limit construct specificity; the splice-discontinuity estimator failed held-out real-speech validation and was dropped.
All 519 recordings and 224 participants are represented; only 2 recordings are dropout-positive and none are frozen-positive, so positive empirical support is sparse or absent.
Exact reconstruction is established, but repeated-recording persistence is zero-dominated and duration/rate pairs are same-ledger summaries rather than independent evidence.
No QTEMP event detector is retained in the validated primary feature set; G9 is therefore not applicable, not failed or pending.

Zero QTEMP features enter the validated primary set. Two dropout summaries are exploratory descriptive outputs, two frozen-audio summaries are monitoring-only zero-variation outputs, and splice is dropped.
